newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Indian diplomat named U.N. envoy in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Indian diplomat named U.N. envoy in Cambodia.

text.p: An Indian former diplomat and academic, Lakhan Mehrotra, was named on Tuesday as the U.N. secretary-general's representative in Cambodia.

The United Nations played a key role in restoring peace to Cambodia after years of internal strife, including genocidal killings by the Khmer Rouge from 1975 to 1979. The country was assisted by a major U.N. peacekeeping operation from 1991 to 1993.

Mehrotra, 62, has served as India's ambassador to a number of countries. He is currently overseas director of the Indian Institute of Culture in New Delhi and a visiting professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University.
He was closely associated with the Cambodia peace process, including the conference that culminated in the 1991 Paris accords.
The previous U.N. representative in Cambodia was Benny Widyono of Indonesia.
